$$f(x) = 7x^{12} + 5x^{9}$$

$$g(x) = -13x^{6} + 4x^{3}$$

The polynomial $q(x)$ is defined as the product of the given polynomials, $f(x)$ and $g(x)$. What is the coefficient of $x^{15}$ in $q(x)$?
explanation: Choice B is correct. The polynomial $q(x)$ is defined as the product $f(x) \cdot g(x) = (7x^{12} + 5x^{9})(-13x^{6} + 4x^{3})$. Applying the distributive property yields $(7x^{12})(-13x^{6}) + (7x^{12})(4x^{3}) + (5x^{9})(-13x^{6}) + (5x^{9})(4x^{3})$. This can be rewritten as $-91x^{18} + 28x^{15} - 65x^{15} + 20x^{12}$. Combining the like terms with $x^{15}$ gives $28x^{15} - 65x^{15} = -37x^{15}$. Therefore, the coefficient of $x^{15}$ in $q(x)$ is $-37$.
